correctness.rationale: The replacement proves the same full ordinary orbit-space classification while deriving the Singer row explicitly from previously published attaching data. Cone each missing Fano-line loop to an outside point; thus all triangle loops in the complete one-skeleton die and the independence complex is simply connected. An independent exhaustive generator-adjunction computation (branches/71688266-17ef-453a-b90f-70f9e1543c18/independent_fano_audit.py; output independent_audit_full.txt lines 1–19) found all 179 subgroups and matches the 12 profiles, all flag-orbit Euler computations, and the four oriented Singer boundary words. Independently, the signed invariant-face counts give Lefschetz Euler values 14, −2, 2, 2, 0; for example an involution fixes three points, acts on three edges pointwise and two by swaps, and stabilizes four triangles with reversed orientation, giving 3−(3−2)−4=−2. Flags of distinct ranks have no inversions. Including the added Sylow-three action arguments at orders twelve and twenty-four, the group labels follow from the census. Only order-seven elements lack geometric fixed points; the stated commutator argument in order 21 and simplicity at order 168 eliminate those elements in the Armstrong quotient outside the order-seven case. Thus the eight order-seven subgroups are exactly the exceptions. For the other cases, Hurewicz and homological Whitehead give wedges of χ−1 two-spheres in this dimension. The repaired Singer proof identifies the same two-skeleton, makes homotopic changes to the other attaching maps before canceling the two generator-defining cells, and leaves two degree-seven disks on a circle; the second is attached along a nullhomotopic loop in the first Moore complex. The original finite checker was inspected without execution; the separate finite enumeration does not formally verify these topological deductions.

value.rationale: The natural finite symmetry family has qualitatively different orbit spaces: contractible, wedges of spheres of several ranks, and one exceptional cyclic type. A complete integral classification tells a researcher exactly when isotropy kills the whole fundamental group and when a free cyclic quotient retains torsion, information not given by the earlier rational table or cyclic calculation. The exact census and topology address the whole subgroup lattice rather than a selected subgroup or a recomputation of known character data.
